ceiling_unlocked: What the item unlocks (row 127 asks for the ceiling, not a gain): throughput -- the same contacts in less wall. ROLL-2's slot capacity was 27.3 % empty (8,997 of 32,909 slot-seconds; docs/results/2026-09-27-slurp-throughput-baseline-and-levers.md), reproduced here to the tenth of a second; the first Solver visit alone waited 2.67 s per row on the client. The model-free bench on the locked PLAN cell measured the empty share 15.56 % -> 10.55 % and 2,736 -> 2,899 contacts per hour of contact window (+6.0 %) under the sealed ROLL-2 per-role service times; the honest bound for a flown cell is about +5 % contacts per GPU-hour on a flown cell (the bench's 0.35 s of wall per row against ROLL-2's flown 7.62 s per row), bounded above by lever 1b's +10.1 % for this mechanism; no number is claimed for lever 1a (the flight's 1,055 s of all-slots-empty time is not reproduced on the bench), and the note's +37.6 % lever-1 bound is not approached.

the_item.default: absent key = every committed configuration = the dispatch exactly as before; the parser refuses unknown keys, a wrong schema, non-boolean switches and a block that arms nothing
the_item.dependency_verified: 1b is POSSIBLE for the recall and IMPOSSIBLE for the rest: the exemplar recall's inputs are the frozen snapshot, the row's own sealed speech query record and the key vectors (rails.phase_supply supply_for_phase -> KbFacetProvider.candidates -> multidim_recall), none of which is the Perception answer; the rank, fusion and the candidate-bound slot-contract selection (candidate_supply.solver, candidate_state_phase perception) DO read the sealed Perception state and stay exactly where they are.
the_item.finding: Rows in flight already exceed the slots (queue depth 4 x slots = 16 admitted rows over 4 slots), but every admitted row is pinned to one llama.cpp slot from its first contact to its delivery, because 88.9 % of the flown prompt tokens are served from that slot's KV prefix; releasing a slot between contacts would re-prefill a row's whole supply block (about 7,500 tokens, 3.3 s) to save a 0.5 s gap. The slots therefore empty while their OWN row prepares the next contact. The largest part of that preparation is the first Solver visit's role input: settle -> the train-exemplars recall (rails.kb_policy.multidim_recall, a pure-Python cosine over every exemplar key vector) -> material, run synchronously in the OpenJiuwen role-query component on the ONE asyncio event loop every row shares, so while one row recalls, no other row can route or dispatch; full garbage collections over the loaded key vectors freeze every thread at once.

switches.gc_freeze: gc.collect(); gc.freeze() before the first episode, gc.unfreeze() after the last
switches.recall_prefetch: the row's Perception-independent recall submitted to one background worker at admission; the Solver visit consumes it through the provider's existing prepared-recall path; a revisit recomputes live
switches.role_input_offload: the role-input builder awaited on ONE dedicated worker thread (role inputs stay mutually exclusive across rows, the calling task's context variables carried over)

throughput_estimate.flown_bound_statement: about +5 % contacts per GPU-hour on a flown cell (the bench's 0.35 s of wall per row against ROLL-2's flown 7.62 s per row), bounded above by lever 1b's +10.1 % for this mechanism; no number is claimed for lever 1a (the flight's 1,055 s of all-slots-empty time is not reproduced on the bench), and the note's +37.6 % lever-1 bound is not approached.
throughput_estimate.service_model: each request holds its slot for a deterministic draw from the sealed ROLL-2 per-role server busy times (launch to release) of the same role
throughput_estimate.statement: On the proof bench (the locked PLAN cell, 60 rows, 285 contacts per run, each request holding its slot for a draw from ROLL-2's own per-role server busy times) the key moved the empty-slot share 15.6 % -> 10.5 % and contacts per hour of contact window 2,736 -> 2,899 (+6.0 %; the two key-on runs +7.3 % and +4.6 %, the two key-off runs within 0.3 %; the sealed pair +6.1 %), removing 1.40 slot-seconds of empty slot and 0.35 s of wall per row; recall_prefetch alone +6.4 %, role_input_offload alone +2.1 %, gc_freeze alone +1.0 %.
